lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 6, in which year did the Ottoman Turks take Constantinople? (1453.) Today: the empire that made it Istanbul, its capital, and spread across three continents.

The Ottoman Empire began about 1299 with Osman, a leader in Anatolia, today's Turkey; the name Ottoman comes from his. In 1453 Sultan Mehmed II took Constantinople. As Istanbul, it was the capital for over 450 years.

At its greatest, under Suleiman the Magnificent (ruled 1520-1566), the empire stretched across three continents: south-east Europe as far as Hungary, western Asia to Baghdad and Mecca, and North Africa from Egypt to Algiers.

Suleiman is remembered in Turkey as the Lawgiver, for his laws. The empire held many peoples and faiths. Christian and Jewish communities could follow their own religion and run many of their own affairs, paying a special tax.

The architect Mimar Sinan (about 1490-1588) designed over 300 buildings. His Süleymaniye Mosque in Istanbul, finished in 1557, has a great dome held up by half-domes, and tall, pencil-shaped minarets. He called the Selimiye Mosque in Edirne his masterpiece.

Istanbul was a great trading city between two seas. Iznik tiles glowed with blue, turquoise and red flowers, especially tulips. Coffee houses opened in the 1550s, where people met to talk. Tulip bulbs travelled from the empire to the Netherlands.

Ottoman armies were strong, and for centuries wars won and lost land; they reached Vienna in 1529 but did not take it. The empire slowly weakened and ended in 1922, and in 1923 Turkey became a republic.
Try it in the world: build a domed mosque with half-domes, two tall, pencil-shaped minarets and a courtyard of blue and white tiles. Next: Mughal India.

exercises.prompt: Which city became the Ottoman capital after 1453?
Which sultan was called the Magnificent?
exercises.hint: In Turkey he is also called the Lawgiver.

exercises.prompt: At its greatest, the Ottoman Empire reached three continents.
exercises.hint: Think of Hungary, Baghdad and Egypt.

exercises.explain: Mimar Sinan, the Ottoman chief architect.

exercises.prompt: Where does the name Ottoman come from?
exercises.explain: From Osman, who began the empire about 1299.

exercises.prompt: Suleiman ruled from 1520 to 1566. For how many years?
exercises.hint: Take the first year from the last.

exercises.prompt: The Ottoman Empire lasted from about 1299 to 1922. For about how many years?
exercises.hint: Take the earlier year from the later one.

exercises.prompt: Match each person to what they did.
exercises.hint: One built, one made laws, one took a city, one began it all.
exercises.explain: Sinan: mosques. Suleiman: the Lawgiver. Mehmed II: Constantinople, 1453. Osman: the name.

exercises.prompt: Sort these cities of the Ottoman Empire by continent.
exercises.hint: Look at the map: Europe north-west of Istanbul, Asia east, Africa south across the sea.
exercises.explain: Europe: Belgrade, Athens. Asia: Baghdad, Mecca. Africa: Cairo, Algiers.

exercises.prompt: What holds up the sides of the great dome in Sinan's mosques?
exercises.hint: Look for the smaller curved roofs beside the dome.
exercises.explain: Half-domes carry the great dome's weight down on each side.

exercises.prompt: How did the Ottomans rule so many peoples of different faiths?
exercises.hint: Think of Christian and Jewish communities in the empire.
choices: faiths could keep their own religious laws
each city chose its own sultan
exercises.explain: Faith communities could follow their own religion and run many of their own affairs, paying a special tax.
False: they reached Vienna in 1529 but did not take it.

exercises.prompt: Sinan was born about 1490 and died in 1588. About how old was he when he died?
exercises.hint: Take the birth year from the year he died.

exercises.prompt: Put these in order, earliest first.
exercises.hint: The smaller the year, the earlier.

exercises.prompt: Why did Istanbul grow rich from trade?
exercises.hint: Look at where it stands on the map.
choices: it stood where Europe meets Asia
it was far from the sea
exercises.explain: It stood where Europe meets Asia, on the strait between two seas, so trade passed through it.
